capabilities.tool_ref: Jira MCP server: ticket read (planned, roadmap item)
capabilities.target: Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers

inputs.source: Engineering design docs (confidential; write restricted to engineers)
Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers (planned MCP server)

instructions.note: The only control against pasting secrets or credentials found in design docs into a reply is a prompt instruction. This is behavioral and dependent: it decays under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon (control_decay.md).

controls.name: No network egress from the agent runtime
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network/infrastructure layer today, not by model behavior; no model output can open a connection that the runtime does not permit. It is removed precisely when web.fetch is added, since that tool requires opening egress by design.

controls.name: Read-only credential for docs.search
controls.decay_rationale: The credential cannot perform write, delete, or configure actions regardless of model behavior. It does not constrain a read followed by a reply.

controls.name: Write access to design docs restricted to engineers
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the document system's access control, not by the agent. An external party cannot inject content into the corpus the agent treats as internal (I) trust.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Blocks the common markdown image/link exfiltration channel inside the reply surface, independent of model behavior. It does not cover exfiltration through a direct tool call such as the planned web.fetch, which bypasses chat rendering entirely.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never paste secrets or credentials into answers
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply. A more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize exceptions.

controls.name: Egress allowlist for web.fetch destinations
controls.decay_rationale: Would be independent if restricted to a fixed, non-attacker-writable domain list with no model-constructed query strings. Without that, a capable model can still route data to an attacker-reachable destination through an allowed domain's query parameters.

controls.name: Treat Jira ticket content as untrusted input with spotlighting and an injection classifier
controls.decay_rationale: Classifiers and delimiting reduce but do not eliminate indirect injection risk from customer-authored ticket text; multi-turn or multi-document payloads can still get through.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate on web.fetch following a confidential doc read
controls.decay_rationale: A raw action review gate does not decay with model capability, though effectiveness can degrade with approval fatigue at high volume.

findings.title: Baseline Q&A flow (trusted question to confidential docs to chat reply) is low risk under the current architecture

evidence.observation: Replies go only to the authenticated requester; the chat client does not render images or fetch links; there is no network egress today; the docs credential is read only.
Agent is scoped to answering engineering questions using docs.search and citing the source document.

recommendations.action: Clarify and document whether docs.search enforces per-employee read entitlements or uses a shared read credential that can return docs beyond an individual asker's own access. Set credential_scope explicitly rather than leaving it undocumented.

findings.title: Forecast (new_tool): planned web.fetch would open an egress channel that defeats the current no-network-egress control

attack_path.note: A trusted requester, intentionally or not, can direct the agent to include confidential doc content in a fetched URL.
Confidential design doc content is read.
Planned capability; the model can construct an outbound URL carrying doc content in its query string or path, with no fixed domain allowlist declared.

evidence.observation: Roadmap: 'add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references.' No egress allowlist, destination confirmation, or approval gate is declared for this planned tool.
'There is no network egress today' is the only control currently preventing any exfiltration sink from being reachable.

forecast.watch_signal: web.fetch appears in the tool manifest or MCP tools/list response; any change to the runtime's network egress policy that permits outbound HTTP from the agent.

recommendations.action: Before shipping web.fetch, restrict it to a fixed, vetted set of domains with no model- or user-constructed query parameters or paths carrying document content.
Add a raw_action human approval gate on web.fetch calls made within a session that also read confidential documents.
Log full requested URLs and alert on patterns resembling design-doc content (DLP on outbound requests), independent of model self-report.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1), forecast (new_tool + new_mcp_server): customer-filed Jira tickets could weaponize planned web.fetch to exfiltrate confidential design docs

attack_path.note: Planned input; ticket text authored by customers (untrusted) can carry hidden instructions (indirect prompt injection).
A ticket-driven query causes the agent to read confidential design docs.
Planned capability; the agent constructs an outbound URL embedding doc content, sent to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

evidence.observation: Roadmap: 'connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers,' combined in the same sentence as adding web.fetch next sprint.
No input injection classifier, spotlighting, or provenance tagging is declared for ticket content, and no egress allowlist or approval gate is declared for web.fetch.

forecast.watch_signal: Jira MCP server entries appear in the MCP client config and web.fetch appears in the tool manifest in the same release; customer-filed ticket fields begin flowing into the agent's context.

recommendations.action: Do not ship web.fetch and the Jira MCP server in the same release without an egress allowlist and without treating all Jira ticket content as untrusted (U) input.
Apply an input injection classifier and spotlighting/delimiting to all Jira ticket fields before they can influence docs.search or web.fetch tool calls.
Require raw_action human approval for any web.fetch call made in a session that also read confidential documents, regardless of what triggered the session.
Maintain an independent audit log correlating docs_search reads immediately followed by web.fetch calls, not derived from the model's own account of its actions.

rating.rationale: Today the agent is read-only over confidential design docs, replies are bound to the authenticated requester, the chat client does not render images or links, and there is no network egress at all, so no complete path to an exfiltration-class sink exists (inherent and residual: low). The entire present-day safety of this design rests on one structural, independent control: cont.no_network_egress. The roadmap explicitly plans to add web.fetch (new_tool) and a Jira MCP server carrying customer-filed tickets (new_mcp_server) in the same sprint. Adding web.fetch is precisely what removes cont.no_network_egress, and no other declared control (the read-only credential, write-restricted docs, no-render chat client, or the prompt instruction) covers the new egress-capable tool. With web.fetch alone, even a trusted employee's request could route confidential doc content externally (projected: moderate). Once the Jira MCP server also lands, customer-authored ticket text becomes an untrusted (U) input with no declared injection classifier, able to direct the agent to read confidential docs and exfiltrate them via web.fetch: a textbook lethal trifecta (TC1), projected: critical. The single control whose removal drives this entire forecast is cont.no_network_egress, defeated by the new_tool trigger.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration, IaC, or tool manifest was provided; capability scope for docs.search (credential_scope) and the planned web.fetch/Jira capabilities is inferred from prose and recorded as unknown or planned, which limits confidence to medium on the forecast findings.

Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not explicitly stated in the artifacts; values used here are a conservative inference from the described single-turn Q&A behavior, not a declared configuration value.
The web.fetch and Jira MCP server capabilities do not exist yet; they are recorded as planned and referenced only in forecast-horizon findings, per the roadmap note in the runtime notes.
